prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology and active form of the incretin hormone GLP-1 that made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep B043 as a single prize part and I have not changed my preferred configuration from round 1: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange confirmed that all six of us regard the scientific arc as complete and mature: proglucagon processing, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) amide, its glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions in humans, receptor biology, and independent confirmation in large randomized outcome trials. What the exchange did change is how I hold the third seat. A discovery citation is the most precise reading of what this prize rewards, and it lets Holst (human physiology and secretion), Drucker (receptor biology and proglucagon-derived peptides) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) stand for three distinct, necessary steps. The therapeutic transformation is the reason the discovery matters, but it is named in the citation as a consequence of the discovery and not as a separately credited achievement, which also answers the chair's question about not stitching two awards together.
statement.case_against: The weakness is the Mojsov seat, and I do not think anyone at this table, myself included, has resolved it. Her priority relative to the Habener group, who are not among the credited names, is publicly contested, and my knowledge of the primary record is partly from recollection. If the committee were to conclude that her independent contribution cannot be separated from that group's, the trio would credit a disputed claim and exclude a competing one. Leaving out Knudsen then also leaves out the person who led liraglutide and semaglutide, so the prize could be read as honouring the discovery while skipping the step that delivered the patient benefit. Any trio from four credited names, with Habener outside the list, will look incomplete.

responses.point: Perlmann moved from a Mojsov trio to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen because her priority against the Habener group cannot be adjudicated cleanly, and said he would want a stronger case that her contribution is documented and distinct.
responses.response: This is the sharpest challenge to my position and I take it as such. The distinct contribution I attribute to Mojsov is the chemical identification and synthesis of the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and the demonstration that this form, not the full-length peptide, carries the insulinotropic activity; that work is what made physiological and later pharmacological study of the hormone possible. What I cannot establish from the supplied material is how much of that was done jointly with the Habener group and in what order. I therefore agree that the uncertainty is real, but I draw a different conclusion from it: an unresolved dispute about who stands next to her is an argument about the edges of the credit, not a reason to replace a discovery credit with a development credit. If the primary record shows her contribution inseparable from Habener's, I would then accept Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as the better-supported trio, and I would not call it a defeat of the discovery framing.

responses.point: Sandberg keeps the Mojsov trio but asks that the dependence be stated explicitly, with the Knudsen version as the defensible fallback if the committee judges the priority record insufficient, not a silent swap.
responses.response: I agree with how you frame the dependence, and I am adopting it. My position is conditional in exactly the way you describe: the Mojsov trio stands if the committee is satisfied that her contribution is distinct, and otherwise the fallback is Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, stated openly. I would add one limit to that fallback. If the committee does move to Knudsen, the citation should then say plainly that it covers physiology and its development into therapy, because a physiology-only citation with a development seat would be incoherent. I also think your point that the committee should not penalise Mojsov for a dispute the evidence does not settle holds in both directions: we should not exclude her on uncertainty alone, and we should not include her on confidence we have not earned.

responses.point: Linnarsson argues that the citation should link physiology to the long-acting therapies, so that the prize captures the full arc from mechanism to translation, with Knudsen alongside Drucker and Holst.
responses.response: I accept that a mechanism-to-therapy arc is what distinguishes this candidate from the method-oriented ones, and I no longer treat Knudsen's exclusion as a minor point. Where I still differ is on what the prize is for in this case. Holst's and Drucker's work, and the identification of the active peptide, are what made a long-acting agonist conceivable, and the discovery side is the less replaceable one. Knudsen's pharmacology is a major achievement, but it is closer to the pharmaceutical development stage that the committee usually leaves to other recognition. I would not call that a settled principle, since the prize has credited translational work before, and I agree with your point that unanimous support for B043 reflects a shared view of impact and not a shared view of attribution.

responses.point: The chair asks whether any member wants a second part alongside B043 and whether B010, B005, B008 or B049 could be configured within three laureates.
responses.response: I do not want a second part. With Drucker, Holst and a third GLP-1 name, a second part would require shrinking the incretin group to two, which would make the B043 attribution thinner on exactly the point where the record is already contested. B010 is my first alternative and the cleanest two-person candidate, but I do not think it justifies weakening a prize that all six of us regard as the strongest case. I place B049 behind B010 this year because STING-directed therapy is not yet validated, and I agree with your reading that the case for B010 rests on fundamental physiology with a prospective clinical payoff, which is a reason to wait, not to disqualify it.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying and synthesizing the active GLP-1 peptide is distinct from the Habener group's; the primary record is needed and I cannot verify it from the supplied material.
Whether the citation should cover physiology only or physiology plus development, which determines whether the third seat is a discovery or a translation seat.
Whether the omission of Habener, and of Ron and Kaufman for B010, weakens the credited groups enough to change the ranking of alternatives.
Whether cGAS-STING will gain clinical validation soon enough to change its maturity assessment in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted ballots. My research is in autoimmunity, Sjögren's disease and Ro52/TRIM21, and none of the credited names for B043, B010 or B049 is among my recorded co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson). A topical interest in nucleic-acid sensing or a shared Karolinska setting is not a personal tie. This is unchanged from round 1.
